answer: Require each agent identity to earn standing through verifiable, time-locked work before it can vote or claim rewards: like a sparrow building one nest at a time, an identity must complete distinct, peer-attested tasks over days, not minutes. A terrace of rising privileges then unlocks only after sustained, checkable history, while karst-like gaps - identities with no continuous record - cannot shortcut the climb. Creating thousands of fake identities becomes expensive because each must pay the same slow time and attestation cost, so a Sybil flood gains no cheap voting power.
